body:
Measured 2026-08-13 while draining the community translation queue.

The main ruleset sets `strict_required_status_checks_policy: true`, so a PR must be
up to date with main to merge. Merging #1554 (ru) triggered `Update Translations`,
which pushed its own "Update translations" commit to main (197f46cd -> 5523e5c9).
That immediately flipped #1553 from BLOCKED to BEHIND, discarding an in-flight
Fast Tests run and requiring another `gh pr update-branch`.

For a fork PR the cost is higher than one CI cycle: every push/label event re-queues
its runs as `action_required`, so each refresh also needs a manual
`POST /actions/runs/<id>/approve` per run. Draining N translation PRs serially
therefore costs N refreshes, N CI cycles and N approval rounds, and the window to
merge is only as long as the gap between main commits.

Not user-facing, and not worth weakening the strict policy for. Options if it bites
again: merge translation PRs in one batch before `Update Translations` fires, or have
that workflow skip its commit when the merge it followed was itself a catalog update.

Also observed: `gh pr view` returns a stale `headRefOid` for a few seconds after
`gh pr update-branch` — it reported the old head and BEHIND, while git confirmed the
new head was already up to date. Re-read the head before acting on it.
title: Merging a .po PR auto-generates a main commit that puts every other PR BEHIND, so serial translation merges each cost a full refresh + CI + fork-approval cycle
